newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil wage ruling shows need for fiscal vigilance.
newsitem.headline: Brazil wage ruling shows need for fiscal vigilance.

text.p: A ruling by Brazil's highest court to grant a 28.9 percent wage rise to 11 civil servants highlights the need for constant vigilance over federal spending, the Presidency said Thursday.

The Presidency said in a statement it would not allow the decision, the impact of which it said it must still evaluate, to hamper the government's drive to cut costs or undermine the 30-month-old "Plano Real" economic stabilization plan.

"The present decision and the hypothesis that a similar interpretation could be repeated in future actions confirm the need for and urgency of the approval of civil service and pension reforms (in Congress)," it said.
It added, "They also demand an additional rigor by the government in the control of public spending in general and of reasonable levels of expenditure on payroll in particular.

"The government reaffirms its determination not to allow...the impact of possible judicial decisions on public payroll spending to compromise the fiscal performance targets necessary for the continuation of the Plano Real."
The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) ruled Wednesday in favor of 11 civil servants who claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent wage rise awarded to the armed forces in 1993.

The ruling could extend to the rest of the public sector workforce, benefiting up to one million current and retired civil servants and costing the government an additional $5.0 billion a year in payroll and $20 billion in backdated pay.
